raw_plan.interpretation: One acquisition email brief for the dossier-qualified slice of the selected audience: freelancers beginning a focused client project and wanting a paper-based 16-week planning structure. The reader relationship is unknown, so the email will make a self-contained, mechanism-led offer and use the documented product-personalisation action rather than assume prior engagement.

intent.reason_now: The reader is beginning a focused 16-week push on a client project.
intent.desired_action: Personalise the Your Plans on Paper planner and add it to the basket.

raw_plan.reader: A freelancer beginning a focused client project who wants a bounded planning structure away from screens.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A goal-driven professional starting a focused 16-week push and wanting planning away from screens
raw_plan.reader_profile_override: Apply the current dossier's narrower qualification: address freelancers delivering a client project, without generalising the fit to all goal-driven professionals.
raw_plan.promise: One client project can have its own 16-week paper planning structure, with undated pages, clear goal breakdowns and accountability tracking tools.
raw_plan.orientation: An undated paper productivity planner for freelancers organising a focused 16-week client project with goal breakdowns and accountability tracking tools.
raw_plan.arc: In this single email, move the reader from a broad interest in paper planning to judging a concrete 16-week mechanism for one client project, then invite them to personalise the planner.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: The audience is solution-aware, so the email should lead with the documented structure rather than explain the planning category. The narrow freelancer scope makes one client project the concrete planning object. No deadline, current tool, failed attempt or immediate complexity problem is established, so the email should not manufacture urgency or a failing status quo. The maintainability concern is only partially connected to the product and cannot be answered with a simplicity claim; the email instead gives the reader specific features they can judge for themselves.

emails.selection_reason: The documented 16-week, undated structure directly matches the reader's bounded project cycle, while goal breakdowns and accountability tracking provide a concrete mechanism a solution-aware freelancer can assess without relying on testimonials or promised outcomes.
emails.target_audience: Freelancers delivering a client project within a focused 16-week push and wanting planning away from screens.
emails.job: Earn the purchase consideration by showing how the planner could structure one focused client project, then prompt the reader to personalise it and add it to the basket.
emails.single_idea: Give one client project a defined 16-week place on paper: the planner combines undated pages with clear goal breakdowns and accountability tracking tools.
emails.felt_need: If a planning system becomes too complicated to maintain, it stops being useful.
emails.mechanism: The productivity planner provides 16 weeks of undated pages, clear goal breakdowns and accountability tracking tools. Present these as the documented structure for planning the project, not as proof that the system is simple to maintain or that the project will be completed.
emails.belief_shift: Before: another productivity planner is only a broad promise about becoming more organised. After: this one offers a specific, bounded structure the reader can judge against a single 16-week client project.
must_not_say: Do not claim the planner is simple, effortless or proven to be maintainable.
Do not promise that the reader will complete the client project, meet a deadline, save time, improve productivity or sustain use.
Do not state or imply that the reader currently uses Google Calendar, another app, scattered notes or any other installed planning system.
Do not claim the reader has missed deadlines, abandoned planners or experienced past planning failures.
Do not present the historical single-source maintainability observation as universal or current audience behaviour.
Do not describe the number, format or operation of the accountability tracking tools or goal breakdowns beyond the documented claims.
Do not claim Papier is unique, better than competitors or the only planner offering these capabilities.
Do not add customer testimonials, adoption claims, measured results or social proof.
Do not broaden the argument from freelancers delivering a client project to every professional undertaking a goal.
Do not make price, Sunbleached Dividers, wedding products, photo books, keepsake journals, shipping, sustainability or unrelated Papier ranges part of this email.
Do not describe Papier as replacing calendars, reminders, collaboration tools or all screen-based planning.
Do not call the 30-day contact policy a refund, return or satisfaction guarantee.
emails.objection: Will this become a planning system that is too complicated to keep using? Answer only by showing the limited documented structure and inviting the reader to judge it; do not assert that Papier has proved it is uncomplicated or maintainable.
emails.tone: Encouraging, focused and gently practical; make the paper format feel appealing without drifting into productivity hype.
emails.next_step_decision: Whether to use this Papier planner as the paper planning structure for the reader's next focused 16-week client project.
emails.next_step_value: The action lets the reader personalise and add to the basket a productivity planner documented as having 16 weeks of undated pages, clear goal breakdowns and accountability tracking tools.
emails.next_step_limit: This step does not establish that the planner will be uncomplicated to maintain, fit the reader's wider digital workflow or produce a successful client-project outcome.

events.body:
Give one focused client project its own 16-week place on paper. Papier’s productivity planner lets you create a personalised plan across 16 weeks of undated pages.

Clear goal breakdowns provide a structure for the project, while accountability tracking tools and reflections help you keep track of progress on the page. The weeks are undated, so the plan begins when the project does.

If a planning system only feels worthwhile when its structure stays focused, you can judge this one by what it contains: 16 undated weeks, goal breakdowns, tracking tools and reflections.

Open the personalisation page to make the planner yours and add it to your basket.

events.preview_text: A bounded, undated structure for mapping out the work.
events.body:
For a focused client project, start with the structure itself: **16 weeks** of undated pages, ready to shape around one clear piece of work.

Papier’s productivity planner pairs those pages with clear goal breakdowns and accountability tracking tools. It gives the project a defined place on paper, away from the screen.

If a planning system only earns its place when the structure feels manageable, judge this one by those elements: a bounded timeframe, undated pages, goal breakdowns and tools for tracking accountability.

The link opens the personalisation step for Your Plans on Paper, where you can personalise the planner and add it to your basket.
